target.title: fix: scope ACP search path approvals [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses a problem where users running the ACP client could have a path-bearing `search` request treated the same as a query-only search request, even when that path was outside the active working directory.

AI-assisted change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP permission classifier now applies the same working-directory containment check to path-bearing `search` alias requests that it already applies to file reads. Query-only `search` calls and OpenClaw-owned `web_search` / `memory_search` calls continue to use the read-only search approval path.

## User Impact

Users keep the low-friction behavior for normal ACP search queries, while `search` calls that target paths outside the current workspace now require the same explicit operator approval as other out-of-scope file access.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox focused test run: `run_b1d3f54ab99b` on lease `cbx_2dc5120eeff7` / `quick-lobster`.
- Command: `corepack pnpm test src/acp/approval-classifier.test.ts src/acp/client.test.ts`.
- Result: 2 test files passed; 66 tests passed.

target.title: fix(android): preserve UTF-16 boundaries in notification text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where forwarded Android notification text could contain an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate when a supplementary character crossed the 512-code-unit limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Notification text now truncates at a valid UTF-16 boundary while preserving the existing 512-code-unit cap and blank-value behavior. A focused regression test places an emoji directly across the truncation boundary.

This PR is AI-assisted. The author reviewed the implementation and validation results.

## User Impact

Forwarded Android notification titles and message previews no longer risk malformed text when an emoji or another supplementary Unicode character falls at the truncation boundary.

## Evidence

- `.\gradlew.bat :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.node.DeviceNotificationListenerServiceTest" --console=plain`
  - `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 28s`
- `.\gradlew.bat :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.node.DeviceNotificationListenerServiceTest" --console=plain`
  - `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2s`
- `git diff --check`
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local`
